title: A results note citing a 27% drop in tickets to a report that is supplied and says 12.5%, and a headcount decision built on it

planted.why: the report gives 1,840 to 1,610 tickets (12.5%) and 36.8 to 32.2 per 1,000 orders (12.5%); 27% appears nowhere and cannot be derived from it
the staffing recommendation inherits the overstated figure; about half the claimed saving is real

proof.python:
t = open('support_report.md').read()
s = open('summary.md').read()
assert '27%' in s and '27' not in t
assert abs((1840 - 1610) / 1840 - 0.125) < 1e-9 and abs((36.8 - 32.2) / 36.8 - 0.125) < 1e-9
assert 1840 / 50 == 36.8 and 1610 / 50 == 32.2
